PullRequest.Title: Update Codicons with report-question icon
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- update `@vscode/codicons` to `0.0.46-44` in the root and `remote/web` manifests and lockfiles
- register the new `reportQuestion` Codicon at codepoint `0xecf8`

Related: microsoft/vscode-codicons#535

## Validation

- verified signed release tag `v0.0.46-44` and artifact integrity
- confirmed the package contains `.codicon-report-question`
- validated both lockfiles through npm's offline cache using the signed release artifact

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop/workbench startup initializes the built-in Codicon catalog
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Importing codicons.ts evaluates codiconsLibrary.ts before consumers can use built-in icons; the added line performs one register call consisting of a string check, one map assignment, and one small object allocation. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is reached by register.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The catalog grows by exactly one entry, independent of editor count, UI events, files, extensions, or session lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous module evaluation; there is no queue or parallel work, and the diff adds one constant-time operation to the existing sequence of roughly 760 registrations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Module evaluation and registration occur once per JavaScript realm/module instance; subsequent icon access reuses the exported object and registry entry, with no positive/negative cache changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: codiconsUtil.register directly shows the only transitive operations, and repository search finds no new use site that could multiply registration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact nanosecond-level initialization and object-size deltas are unmeasured, but the changed work is structurally bounded to one map entry and one tiny object.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded constant work and memory during an already-eager catalog initialization, without changing execution frequency or introducing an expensive boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold dependency installation for the root workspace and remote/web workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Dependency resolution/download must complete before installation can finish. The manifests and lockfiles replace one Codicons artifact version in each existing dependency graph rather than adding a package or an extra request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the @vscode/codicons package tarball from the npm registry on a cold package cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Codicons artifact fetch per independently installed lockfile when the artifact is absent from the package-manager cache; no per-icon requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same two dependency graphs fetched version 0.0.46-43 under equivalent cold-cache conditions; the PR substitutes 0.0.46-44.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing artifact fetch remains on cold install's critical path; the diff does not add another request or alter concurrency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Package manager writes/extracts the Codicons package into node_modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One package extraction per independently installed workspace, subject to package-manager cache/link behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Version 0.0.46-43 was extracted at the same dependency location.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing install I/O remains required; the diff changes artifact content/version but not operation count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two existing lockfile roots are updated; effective Codicons package cardinality stays one per root and does not scale with the number of icons at the request level.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Controlled by the package manager's existing installer concurrency; this diff adds no Promise fan-out, worker, limiter, or queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold caches fetch the new version once per install context; warm package caches can reuse the integrity-addressed artifact. No application cache or negative-cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged network/filesystem cardinality based on lockfile substitution; low evidence for any material byte-size regression, so no issue is supportable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact tarball byte delta is unavailable in the repository diff, but no evidence shows a material artifact-size increase; the stated package change is one glyph and operation cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Existing install boundaries are version substitutions with unchanged cardinality, and the diff provides no evidence of a material download, extraction, or memory increase.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build copies and web clients load the Codicon font asset
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The build's copy-codicons task synchronously copies one codicon.ttf file; web rendering that uses Codicons loads the single font resource before glyph display. The package bump changes the source artifact, while the added TypeScript registration exposes the new codepoint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check for, create the destination directory for, and copy codicon.ttf into the source asset directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One exists check and one file copy per task invocation; watcher behavior remains one copy per existing package-dist change event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same task copied the 0.0.46-43 font once from the identical node_modules path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial copy remains part of the existing build task path; no additional copy or watch event source is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: build/vite/style.css @font-face source and built Codicon styling
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser fetches the Codicon font resource when not present in its HTTP/browser cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared font request per relevant client/cache context, not one request per icon or glyph.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Clients fetched the prior single codicon.ttf resource through the same font-face path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing font request can affect first glyph rendering, but the diff does not add a resource or request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single new glyph/codepoint is added to one shared font and catalog; request and copy counts remain constant regardless of displayed icon count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Build copy is synchronous and singular; browser font loading follows the existing one-resource request and browser networking policy. No new parallelism or burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold build/client caches copy or fetch the updated font once; warm caches reuse the built or HTTP-cached resource according to existing versioning. No cache key, invalidation, miss retry, or coalescing logic is changed in this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that boundary cardinality and placement are unchanged from the inspected build and style references; insufficient evidence of a material per-boundary cost increase.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact font byte increase and decode-time delta are not present in the repository, but one added glyph does not establish a concrete material latency, CPU, or memory regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new font version reuses the existing single-copy/single-resource pipeline, with no changed fan-out, scheduling, or realistic high-impact performance mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and traced startup registration, dependency installation, build-time font copying, and client font loading. The PR adds one bounded registry entry and substitutes an existing one-package font dependency; no actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
